column1: # Philosophy: the aim is bigger fish. Weight reflects how much a confirmed population
# raises the value of a hidden reach or lake — not just how popular the species is
# but how hard it is to find
column3: and how much it rewards a long paddle.

column1: # Muskellunge gets 10 because a hidden muskie lake is the whole point of this tool.
# Minnow streams get 1 because they tell you nothing worth hiding.
# Weights are tunable — adjust as fishing goals evolve.
# NOTE: Species names must exactly match ARA FISH_SPECIES_SUMMARY values (case-sensitive).
# Verify after Part 6 ingest: SELECT DISTINCT TRIM(unnest(string_to_array(fish_species_summary
column3: '))) FROM ara_points ORDER BY 1;

Ontario trophy pinnacle. A hidden muskie lake in FMZ 17 is the jackpot this tool is built for. Rare enough that presence is a strong signal.
Primary driver of FMZ 17 value. Most sought-after table fish in Ontario. A hidden walleye body of water that doesn't appear on popular fishing maps is exactly what this tool should surface.
Cold-water indicator species — confirmed presence means deep pristine oligotrophic water. Dominant trophy fish in FMZ 16's deeper lakes. Rare enough to be meaningful.
Native stream trout. Cold clean usually remote. A confirmed wild brook trout stream is one of the best things this tool can surface — the stream equivalent of a trophy lake.
Top sport fish across both FMZs. Not rare but a high-smallmouth hidden reach is genuinely worth finding — especially in FMZ 16's Georgian Bay drainages.
Big pike are legitimate trophy targets. Common but large pike in a hidden bay or backwater are worth the paddle.
Hugely popular widely stocked but also self-sustaining in good river systems. A hidden rainbow river is high-value.
Major Great Lakes tributary run species. Confirmed presence signals a substantial river system with serious sport potential.
Great sport fish often stocked but can naturalize. One tier below brook trout because it's non-native.
Popular and fun but skews toward warmer shallower more accessible water. One tier below smallmouth as a hiddenness signal.
Excellent eating challenging to catch associated with clean cold lakes. Presence alongside lake trout is a very good signal.
Walleye's rare close relative. Historically present in St. Lawrence / Ottawa drainage. High weight because confirmed sauger water is genuinely special.
Great Lakes tributary salmon. One tier below Chinook on size and run magnitude.
Cold-water native excellent eating (ice fishing target). Indicator of deep clean lakes. Under-targeted and often hidden — a confirmed burbot water is a quiet gem.
Sterile Northern Pike x Muskellunge hybrid stocked in some Ontario waters. Worth noting but one tier below true muskellunge.
Lake cisco / lake herring. As a target fish it's modest but confirmed cisco presence strongly implies cold oxygenated deep water — prime lake trout and walleye habitat.
Important ice fishing species good eating. Ubiquitous in FMZ 17 — presence alone is a weak hiddenness signal; weight reflects its value as a quarry.
Genuine sport panfish challenging to find in numbers. Fun when you locate a hidden crappie school.
Specifically targeted by a subset of Ontario anglers. Presence in a hidden backwater is notable.
Less common than black crappie in Ontario similar appeal.
Fun panfish widely distributed. Present almost everywhere so not a strong hiddenness signal on its own.
Niche target; some anglers specifically night-fish for bullheads.
Similar to brown bullhead. Less common in Ontario range.
Least common Ontario bullhead. Same niche target weight.
Under-targeted in Ontario (southeastern distribution). Confirmed drum is interesting to a specific angler.
Common panfish. Low bar for presence.
Rare in Ontario (near southern border). Weight 3 as a panfish curiosity.
Niche — dedicated carp anglers value hidden carp water. Not our primary audience.
Somewhat sought by specialized anglers. Indicator of clean well-oxygenated rivers.
Same rationale as silver redhorse.
Species at risk in Ontario — confirmed presence is ecologically notable even if not a top angling target.
Targeted by dip-netters in spring runs. Fun but not a serious fishing signal.
Rough fish. Ubiquitous — presence tells you almost nothing about water quality or hiddenness.
Same rationale as white sucker.
Carpsucker — rough fish low signal value.
Largest Ontario minnow sometimes mistaken for a gamefish. Niche interest at best.
Common minnow indicator of small creek habitat. Presence confirms it's a stream not much else.
Cold-water minnow often co-occurs with brook trout — the brook trout signal matters more.
Fast-water riffle species. Habitat indicator but not a target.
